text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

-- Hachette Distribution Service, a subsidiary of the French group Lagardere, has agreed to pay $55 million for a 51-percent stake in Poland's news-stand chain Ruch SA. The French company will invest further $45 million in Ruch over the next three years.

-- About 25 percent of Poles think foreign banks should not face any barriers when opening branches in Poland, according to a survey by the PBS institute. Some 38 percent think foreign banks should be allowed to buy Polish financial institutions, the poll showed.
-- Chemical trader Ciech SA will submit a prospectus of its new share issue to the Securities Commission by the end of 1996.
-- Foregin companies have committed themselves to invest $8 billion within the next six year, according to the government Agency for Foreign Investment.
-- Italy's Fiat will invest $800 million in its Polish subsidiaries to launch production of new cars.
